paths.title: Reliable API Contracts
paths.description: Design predictable request, response, error, pagination, and retry behavior.
concept: An API contract includes failure behavior
A dependable endpoint defines inputs, outputs, status codes, authentication, limits, and error shapes.
Clients become fragile when validation, not-found, conflict, rate-limit, and server errors are inconsistent.
workflow: Write the contract in a form that can be tested.
A concrete contract reduces ambiguity between frontend, backend, and external consumers.
List success and failure status codes.
Turn each rule into a test.
question: Use the correct conflict response
A request tries to create a username that already exists. Which status best describes the outcome?
200 OK
201 Created
409 Conflict
503 Service Unavailable
409 communicates that the request conflicts with the current state of the target resource.
checklist: Check that clients can handle every endpoint predictably.
Success and error bodies follow stable shapes.
Versioning and deprecation rules are documented.

paths.title: Data Integrity and Concurrency
paths.description: Protect invariants when multiple requests read and modify shared data.
concept: Two individually correct requests can corrupt state when they read and write the same data concurrently.
Transactions, constraints, atomic operations, isolation, and idempotency protect invariants that application checks alone cannot guarantee.
workflow: Design the operation around the invariant that must remain true.
Start with the business rule, then choose the database mechanism that enforces it under concurrency.
Choose an atomic statement or transaction.
Detect stale writes with versions or locks.
question: Prevent a lost update
Two clients edit the same record. Which mechanism detects that one client saved an outdated version?
A larger response body
Optimistic concurrency with a version column
A CSS class
A longer URL
A version comparison rejects stale writes instead of silently overwriting newer data.
checklist: Verify that invalid partial states cannot be committed.
Important invariants should be enforced close to persistent state.
Idempotency is defined for retried commands.

paths.title: Operations and Observability
paths.description: Run services with health checks, structured telemetry, graceful shutdown, and recoverable deployments.
concept: Logs, metrics, and traces should explain what a request did, where time was spent, and why it failed.
Telemetry must be structured, correlated, bounded in volume, and scrubbed of secrets.
workflow: Capture enough context to diagnose failures without recording sensitive data.
Use a request identifier across entry, downstream calls, and completion.
Assign or accept a correlation identifier.
Link alerts to dashboards and runbooks.
question: Separate liveness and readiness
What should a readiness check answer?
Whether the process exists
Whether the service can currently perform required work
Whether the source code is formatted
Whether all historical requests succeeded
Readiness determines whether traffic should be routed to the instance.
checklist: Confirm that the service can fail and recover safely.
Operational controls should be tested before an incident.
Liveness and readiness have distinct meanings.
